raw_response:
I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou, this is the system I know best, it fits my soil, water, and machinery, and it gives me the safest income. I do not want to scatter my effort across too many crops. I will finish the winter wheat already in the field, then plant summer maize right after harvest. For seed, I will use stable improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I care more about steady yield and easier management than trying something unfamiliar. On fertilizer, I will feed wheat a bit more steadily through the season and give maize enough nitrogen for strong growth, but I will not push too hard because too much fertilizer wastes money and can make lodging and disease worse. On water, I will irrigate wheat more carefully because it needs support at key stages, while maize will get fewer irrigations unless the summer turns dry. I will keep pesticide use moderate and spray only as needed for the common local weeds, aphids, rusts, and corn pests. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage for wheat establishment and no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest because that saves time and helps me catch the planting window. My goal is not the highest possible yield on paper; my goal is a crop I can manage well and harvest safely.
